value: Cohort of 10 subjects; half received allogenic FMT from one of three lean donors, half received autologous FMT (placebo).
55 fecal samples sequenced from FMT metabolic syndrome study; compared to 109 metagenomes from 48 healthy FMT-naive individuals.
42 species across five phyla analyzed for determinant SNV positions; 11.8 million variant positions across 1105 detected prokaryotic species.
Same-donor recipients (FMT1, 2, 3) showed differing donor-strain retention: 12.0%, 46.1%, 56.6% respectively at 3 months.

host_species.evidence_quote: donor strains can colonize in the human gut after bowel lavage
host_species.notes: Study involves human FMT recipients (metabolic syndrome patients) and human donors.

extraction_warnings: This paper is a strain-level metagenomic reanalysis of an existing FMT clinical cohort (Vrieze et al. 2012); many demographic/clinical fields (age, sex, country, ancestry, dna_extraction_kit, sequencing_platform) are not reported in the provided text and may be documented only in the original clinical trial paper or supplementary methods not included here.
Per-sample identifiers (e.g., FMT1-5, SELF1-5, CTRL1-5) exist in figures but without accompanying per-sample demographic data, so sample-level rows were not constructed to avoid fabrication.

The 'control' field values were inferred from study design description (allogenic=Case, autologous=placebo/Study Control, healthy=external Study Control) rather than an explicit statement using this terminology; confidence set to medium.
Days from first collection vary across multiple time points (e.g., 2, 14, 42, 84 days) and could not be reduced to a single study-level value without fabricating sample-level granularity.

Batch 1 subgroups ['allogenic FMT recipient', 'placebo (autologous FMT) recipient', 'donor', 'healthy control'] differ from batch 0 ['Allogenic FMT recipients', 'Autologous FMT recipients (placebo)', 'Healthy controls']; kept batch 0.
fmt_role is an enum field but the study includes multiple roles (donor, recipient before/after) per subject over time; value set to 'other' with detailed by_subgroup breakdown.
No specific age, BMI, or dietary details were reported for participants in the main text provided.
Healthy control identifiers (CTRL1-5) were inferred from Figure 1 axis labels, not explicit running text.
Batch 2 returned granularity='study_level', differs from batch 0 ('subgroup_level'); kept batch 0.
Batch 2 subgroups [] differ from batch 0 ['Allogenic FMT recipients', 'Autologous FMT recipients (placebo)', 'Healthy controls']; kept batch 0.

Schema fields (biomarker_*, disease_response_os, ecog_performance_status, feces_phenotype_value, tumor_size_*) appear designed for oncology/clinical biomarker studies and are largely not applicable to this microbiome/FMT strain-tracking paper.
uncurated_metadata was populated with study-level descriptive details since no closer-matching schema field existed; treat as supplementary context rather than a standardized extracted variable.
No per-sample rows from the article's own tables; falling back to the SRA/ENA run manifest (1 table(s)).
Table 'PRJEB12357_ena_manifest.tsv': re-attached plan-dropped schema column(s) instrument_model→sequencing_platform for downstream mapping.
Fanned out 5160 cell(s) of study/subgroup-level field values into per-sample rows.
